claim.text: The rejected Gen19 eager two-clause continuation policy has heterogeneous effects on externally documented list relations, including moderate slowdowns for repeated ground calls but little difference in many one-shot relational queries, while preserving selected finite-list answers.
claim.scope: Twelve externally documented relation tasks reconstructed for the Rust finite Horn subset plus two unchanged-path null controls; native ELF64/i686, pinned Rust 1.85.1, 20 samples/version/case/ABI.
assumptions: Published list relations correspond to the reconstructed finite Horn subset under a declared answer order
Python list-algebra oracle is independent from Rust implementation but project-authored
Both frozen engines are separately compiled from immutable Gen18 and Gen19 commits
forbidden_promotions: No independently authored benchmark code or independent experimental study
No universal Prolog or WAM performance claim
No full ISO/GNU Prolog semantic conformance
No causal CPU-time partition from earlier DHAT/Callgrind site labels

specification.intended_object: A source-linked, finite-list semantic and native-time comparison of two immutable Rust solver ownership representations.
invariants: 14 full Python-reference output and exit/stderr comparisons per ABI
264 full historical Rust CLI differential cases per ABI
20 raw direct-solve samples per version/case/ABI in five alternating AB/BA blocks
Two unrelated null controls within [0.8,1.2] ratio on each ABI
known_answer_cases: single fact and builtin true null controls

implementation.commit: released Gen18 901c8b58c12fbe8b79f70b0118f951f3ed2fcf21 vs retired Gen19 c09fff05d9b3dd43fb90014278e3a98d701d3640
implementation.environment: Ubuntu 24.04 native ELF64 and true i686 ELF32, pinned Rust 1.85.1 release with feature disabled, Python 3 standard library mathematical oracle
implementation.live_entrypoint: gprolog_native::solve() via shared external bench_continuations.rs, plus gprolog-rs CLI exact stdout/stderr/exit
implementation.representation: Fourteen source/query SHA256-provenance cases, complete ordered answer oracle and raw matched timing vectors

metric.name: Typed case-by-architecture direct-solve ratio and independent-reference ordered-answer correctness
metric.units: nanoseconds, unitless ratios, paired block win counts and exact stdout/stderr/exit
equivalence_attacks: Same relation with ground repeated vs variable single-query form
Null single fact and builtin control

264 frozen strict full-output Rust CLI comparisons per ABI

Duplicate select alternatives and prefix enumeration order

matched_baselines: Immutable Gen18 baseline vs retired unmerged Gen19 built with same compiler flags/ABI and external harness
controls.compute_parity: Same host ABI, compiler, flags and external harness within pairs; separately report architectures.
controls.parameter_parity: Same source/query bytes, max steps, max solutions and repeat factor per case.
controls.sampling_parity: 5 paired alternating AB/BA blocks and 4 timed calls per variant/block, 3 unmeasured warmups per process.
controls.data_access_parity: Same source task URLs, source SHA256, program and query strings, oracle code and fixed case selection.

preregistration.prediction: A large synthetic 8–11x regression need not transfer uniformly; some recursive list/failing-first-goal cases may be slower, without a numerical speedup/slowdown claim fixed in advance.
preregistration.primary_metric: All twelve external relation case ratios and per-block win counts on each native ABI, without scalar collapse; two unrelated controls [0.8,1.2].
preregistration.uncertainty_method: 20 raw solve samples per variant/case/ABI, five paired blocks; descriptive geometric mean and block directions only; no external random sample or adjusted inferential confidence.
preregistration.kill_condition: Any Python truth-oracle output mismatch, unsupported parser semantics, source hash divergence, invalid timing sample or unchanged-path null control outside [0.8,1.2].
preregistration.stop_condition: Never tune fixtures to a desired performance sign or change either interpreter to rescue a failed experiment.
preregistration.promotion_rule: M for exact bounded result vector and reference correctness only after both native ABIs and final-head CI; no claim of unbiased external-Prolog generalization.

result.observed: Both native ABIs passed 14/14 Python answer-oracle cases and 264/264 historical strict CLI cases; all timing/negative controls passed. Of twelve published-relation cases, Gen19 slower medians in 10 ELF64 and 9 i686, >=4/5 slower blocks in 5 ELF64 and 6 i686; five cases show same >=4/5 slowdown direction across both. Maximum observed ratio 1.404303 ELF64 and 1.376968 i686.
result.effect_size: Complete signed fourteen-case tuple in CSV; descriptive geometric mean of twelve relation ratios: 1.078411 ELF64 / 1.079179 i686; no universal speed effect.
result.uncertainty: Externally documented relations but author reconstructed code, author-written Python list oracle, curated educational subset; 5 blocks/ABI, no independent Prolog implementation or external author reproduction.
retired_claims: Uniform 8-11x synthetic regression transfer to every two-clause Prolog program
Conflating publicly documented relations with independently authored executable workloads
active_remainder: True third-party authored licensed Prolog programs
Independent SWI/GNU Prolog semantic execution reference
Real-world workloads with missing/unsupported language features recorded separately
